# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# fields: COMMAND_RPC_SWEEP_ALL's response is split_transfer_response,
#         src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:634-661 -- EVERY FIELD IS A LIST:
#           tx_hash_list, tx_key_list, amount_list, amounts_by_dest_list (OPT, :652),
#           fee_list, weight_list, tx_blob_list, tx_metadata_list,
#           multisig_txset string, unsigned_txset string, spent_key_images_list
#         amounts_by_dest_list[] = amounts_list (:556-565) = { amounts: [u64] }
#         spent_key_images_list[] = key_image_list (:547-554) = { key_images: [string] }
# NO status/untrusted.
# TWO TRANSACTIONS, deliberately: DESIGN.md §8 Phase 0 asks for "a split_transfer_response with TWO
#   transactions, so the list path is exercised". A one-entry list would let a consumer that reads
#   only [0] pass every test, and §2a.4's partial-sweep rule -- "a relay_tx that fails at entry k of
#   N aborts the loop, drops the metadata of entries k..N, leaves the record in place and exits 16
#   naming 'k-1 of N broadcast'" -- would have no N > 1 to be written against. send::relay calls
#   relay_tx ONCE PER ENTRY of tx_metadata_list, IN ORDER, under one pending.json record.
# ALL EIGHT LISTS ARE INDEX-ALIGNED, and nothing on the wire enforces that. Entry i's hash, amount,
#   fee, weight, metadata and key images are tx_hash_list[i], amount_list[i], fee_list[i],
#   weight_list[i], tx_metadata_list[i], spent_key_images_list[i]. §5c turns them into ONE array of
#   objects (`txs`), never parallel arrays, precisely because two arrays that must stay in lockstep
#   are two arrays that will not.
# tx_key_list AND tx_blob_list ARE EMPTY LISTS, not lists of empty strings: the request sends
#   get_tx_keys: false and get_tx_hex: false (:909, :912), and upstream only pushes onto those lists
#   when the corresponding flag is set. THE TRANSACTION SECRET KEY IS A SECRET (§2b.2) and fmonero
#   never asks for it.
# THE REQUEST ALWAYS CARRIES subaddr_indices_all: true (§2a.10), and SweepRequest has no field that
#   could turn it off. With it absent (KV_SERIALIZE_OPT default FALSE, :903) and subaddr_indices
#   empty, on_sweep_all hands an EMPTY SET to create_transactions_all (:1786-1795), which then picks
#   ONE SUBADDRESS AT RANDOM -- "in case subaddress index wasn't specified, choose non-empty
#   subaddress randomly (with index=0 being chosen last)" (src/wallet/wallet2.cpp:11846-11853). A
#   command documented as the way to empty an account would move one random subaddress's funds,
#   report success, and leave the rest. NO FIXTURE CAN CATCH THAT: this file is served either way.
#   The assertion is on the RECORDED REQUEST in the --log file, and §2a's test list says so.
# `outputs` defaults to 1 for sweep_all (KV_SERIALIZE_OPT (uint64_t)1, :906), which is the value
#   fmonero wants, so it is never sent. COMMAND_RPC_TRANSFER has no `outputs` field at all in
#   0.18.5.1 (:596-627).
# AMOUNTS: the two transactions sweep 1234567891234 - 61440000 = 1234506451234 piconero in total
#   (the balance of get_balance.json less both fees), split 800000000000 + 434506451234. The fees are
#   the 30720000 of transfer-do-not-relay.json each, so a consumer summing fee_list gets 61440000 and
#   §5's PendingStatus.total_fee_pico has a non-trivial sum to compute with Piconero::checked_add.
# tx_metadata values are 512-character deterministic hex blobs, distinct per entry and distinct from
#   transfer-do-not-relay.json's, so a test that relays the wrong entry fails on the bytes.
#   They are NOT real serialized pending_tx structures -- no mock can produce one.
